query: Help me understand what's in these airline reviews — I'm not sure which aspect is most worth analyzing.

per_column.name: primary_complaint_category
per_column.rationale: As a topical grouping axis (service, ground ops, baggage, pricing, food, etc.) this genuinely helps an analyst decide which aspect dominates the corpus, which is exactly what the exploratory query asks for. Groundedness is undermined by the 'complaint' framing: the evidence shows glowingly positive reviews ('Flight was amazing', 'Excellent performance on all fronts') all forced into 'service_quality' as a complaint, when no complaint exists in the text. The topic tag is defensible, but asserting a complaint where the source records praise is an over-assertion.

per_column.name: sentiment_polarity
per_column.rationale: This is essentially a graded positive/negative sentiment flag, which the rubric explicitly flags as low-leverage, and it is largely redundant with the existing 'Overall Rating' and 'Recommended' columns. It offers little new axis to model on. Values themselves are well grounded in the samples (amazing→highly_positive, dreadful seats→negative, excellent→positive), so groundedness is high even though usefulness is weak.

per_column.name: crew_interpersonal_demeanor
per_column.rationale: A qualitative crew-behavior axis (rude/indifferent/friendly/professional) is a useful complement to the numeric Staff Service score and helps profile a key aspect. However groundedness is poor: only 100 NULLs across ~8000 rows means the column asserts a crew demeanor almost everywhere, including the seat-discomfort review that never mentions crew at all yet was labeled 'indifferent_robotic'. That is an invented reading of a silent source, indicating systematic over-assertion.

per_column.name: operational_disruption_type
per_column.rationale: Captures delays, cancellations, baggage failures, missed connections, etc. — a distinct operational axis not present in the original columns and clearly valuable for deciding what to analyze. Grounding looks sound: all five silent samples correctly resolve to 'no_disruption', which is appropriate abstaining behavior rather than fabrication. The heavy 'no_disruption' majority is expected and not a defect.

per_column.name: physical_comfort_details
per_column.rationale: Decomposes seat/aircraft comfort into specific sub-issues (legroom, recline, aircraft age, thermal), adding detail beyond the raw Seat Comfort rating. Values track the text well: 'legroom is spacious' and 'seat far too narrow, poor padding' both map to seat_design_legroom as a topic, and silent/positive rows map to no_issues. It captures the discussed aspect rather than the sentiment, which is acceptable.

per_column.name: cabin_environment_quality
per_column.rationale: A cleanliness/upkeep axis that is not directly represented in the original ratings, so it adds analytical leverage. It does use NULL for many rows, but in the samples it defaults silent reviews (the seat-discomfort review, the 'good service' review that never mentions the cabin) to 'acceptably_clean', asserting a mildly positive cleanliness state the text does not support. The explicit-cleanliness rows (sanitized seat, well-maintained aircraft) are correctly labeled.

judge.rationale: For an open-ended 'which aspect is most worth analyzing' query, the set provides several genuinely distinct aspect axes (complaint topic, crew demeanor, operational disruptions, comfort sub-details, cabin cleanliness) that let the analyst compare and prioritize aspects — this is well matched to the query. The main usefulness drag is sentiment_polarity, a generic sentiment flag largely redundant with the existing Overall Rating/Recommended columns. Groundedness is mixed: sentiment, operational_disruption, and physical_comfort are well anchored, but crew_interpersonal_demeanor fabricates crew judgments for reviews that never mention crew (near-zero NULL rate), cabin_environment_quality defaults silent rows to a positive cleanliness state, and primary_complaint_category imposes a 'complaint' onto plainly positive reviews. These over-assertions on silent/positive sources pull the table-level groundedness down.
